text:
Last wk, $KBWB -1% despite low bank earnings expectations. AI was hit despite beat/raise from
$ASML -8%, $TSM -9% due to AI financing concerns w/ AirTrunk IPO delayed, debt getting hit w/ $CRWV -25%, Anthropic rev growth slowing & valuation looking ~$1.5T vs $2T.

Last Sunday I wrote that I was circumspect on the market. The KBWB (bank ETF) was sending a very different message than the S&P. “Any further sell-off despite trading at oversold levels last week would not be a great sign.” On Tuesday I posted on the KBWB getting hit despite these low expectations on mixed earnings results and therefore remaining circumspect. The Magnificent 7 eventually closed the week down 3.2% with the SOX Index (Semiconductors) down 11.4% driving the S&P down 1.9%.

There was rising angst on the financing part of the AI trade later in the week. This was despite 5/10/30yr yields going down 15-17 bps last week despite hotter than expected CPI/PPI. After yields initially surged, this large drop was unexpected but this also coincided with the equity market sell-off from Wednesday through Friday.

Massive external capital is needed to fund the AI infrastructure buildout. Therefore AI stocks got clobbered last week on questions around:
1) ability to raise AI public equity – Airtrunk IPO delayed till 2027 following the pulling of Firmus IPO last week
2) cost of AI debt increasing- CDS costs surging and face value of debt getting hit driving the yield to 15% for Coreweave debt
3) AI revenue growth slowi

text:
Well, this post struck a nerve.

Calls for a "Black Monday" stock market crash are trending again. Last night, we took the opposite view.

As with every market prediction we make, there are thousands of people urging others to "fade" us.

But take a look at the chart below. It shows every time "Black Monday" has trended on social media since May 2025.

History suggests that calls for a "Black Monday" crash have repeatedly presented some of the best buying opportunities.

And as we outline in our analysis below, the majority of stocks in the S&P 500 have already experienced a bear market, EVEN AS the index trades near record highs; a largely unprecedented occurence.

How is this possible? Read our full analysis here:

https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2110778022131306528
